Previously, at Deloitte India, I contributed to role-based access control, real-time data synchronization, and containerized position assignments, leveraging AngularJS, C#, .NET, and SQL. I have a strong foundation in full-stack development with expertise in:

✔ Programming Languages: C++, C, Java, C#
✔ Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React.js, Angular.js
✔ Backend & Databases: ASP.NET Core, SQL, MySQL, Firebase
✔ Development Tools: GitHub, Visual Studio, VS Code, Postman, SQL Server Management Studio
✔ Key Subjects: Data Structures, Algorithms, Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), Database Management Systems (DBMS), Operating Systems |

Murtaz Khan
Jul 6, 2024
In North America, Work Experience is given more precedence than anything else, so 60-70% (no more than that) of your CV should be covered by work experience

Recruiters love when you prove the knowledge you possess of tools and different skills. This fact is proven through hard figures and examples.

Work experience is usually written like:
“Action verb” + “task” + “strategy/process” + “Result (has to be a metric)”
It doesn’t have to follow this pattern, but it should cover all 4 areas
Eg: “Increased monthly sales by 25% by implementing a targeted email marketing campaign and optimizing ad placement”


How I wrote my points, I put tools/strategies and figures in bold:
Infastructed Gitlab runners to build and test servers to communicate with device clients, while caching to reduce pipeline wait by 300%.


Every area of your work experience should have 3-5 bullet points.

Also when it comes to tailoring your CV, use jargons from your job role and prove those skills for a greater impact.
